To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ALS-associated mutant forms of TDP43, FUS1, and SODG93A inhibit protein transport from ER to Golgi, and that Rab1 is required for ER-Golgi protein transport in cells expressing ALS-mutant proteins, and in motor neurons from ALS patients.
ALS-mutants of TDP-41, FUS, or SOD1 perturb protein transport between the ER and Golgi apparatus, which is mediated by Rab1.

ALS-associated mutant forms of TDP43, FUS (TDP43) and SOD1 (FUS) all perturb protein trafficking between ER and Golgicompartment, and that this is a common pathomechanism for these three diverse disease proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of protein transport between the ER and the Golgi apparatus.
the molecular mechanisms of protein transport in the secretory pathway.
the molecular basis of amyotrophic lateral scelrosis (ALS) and the discovery of novel therapeutic targets for the disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Rab1-dependent ER-GOLGI transport dysfunction is a shared pathogenic mechanism in ALS.
Rab1-dependent ER-GOLGI transport dysfunction is a pathogenic mechanism in ALS, and that this is a common pathomechanism in SOD1-associated, TDP- 43 and FUS associated ALS.
the ER-Goligi transport dysfunction is a shared pathogenic mechanism in ALS, and that this dysfunction is caused by different mechanisms for each of the ALS-linked proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a common pathogenic event in three different forms of ALS, which is mediated by the small GTPase, Rab1, and that this mechanism is a potential therapeutic target for ALS.
we have identified a novel mechanism of neurodegeneration in ALS, and have identified Rab1 as a novel therapeutic target for ALS.
ER-Golgi protein transport is perturbed in the early secreted pathway by ALS-associated mutant proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the early secretory pathways are perturbed in ALS.
the early secretory transport pathway is a common target for ALS-associated proteins, and that Rab1 is a common target that can be used to restore ER-Golgi protein transport.
we have identified a common cellular defect in ALS that can be reversed by a small molecule drug that can be used in clinical trials.
